categories.main_business_segments: Procore operates as a single business segment focused on providing cloud-based construction management software. Its platform is organized into five integrated product categories: Preconstruction, Project Execution, Workforce Management, Financial Management, and Construction Intelligence, all designed to support the construction project lifecycle.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Procore's platform is built on modern, modular, and extensible cloud architecture, accessible via web and mobile applications. It leverages open APIs, a shared services layer, and an App Marketplace for third-party integrations. The company invests heavily in R&D to deliver intuitive, user-centric software, advanced analytics, and AI-driven features, with a focus on real-time collaboration, data centralization, and workflow automation.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Procore primarily serves owners, general contractors, and specialty contractors in the commercial, residential, industrial, and infrastructure construction sectors. Its customers range from small businesses to global enterprises, and the platform is used by a wide array of project stakeholders including architects and engineers.
categories.geographic_coverage: Procore is headquartered in Carpinteria, California, with additional offices across the U.S. and internationally in Australia, Canada, Mexico, England, Singapore, UAE, France, Ireland, and Egypt. As of 2022, it had customers running projects in over 150 countries, with 14% of revenue generated outside the U.S.
categories.supply_chain_position: Procore operates as a downstream technology provider, delivering software solutions directly to end users in the construction industry. It does not manufacture physical goods but enables digital transformation and workflow management for construction project stakeholders.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Procore's strategic priorities include expanding its customer base, increasing product adoption, and international growth. The company invests significantly in R&D to maintain technology leadership, enhance its platform with new features (including AI and analytics), and develop adjacent offerings such as materials financing. Acquisitions and ecosystem expansion through its App Marketplace are also key elements of its strategy.
categories.revenue_model: Procore generates substantially all of its revenue from fixed-fee, subscription-based contracts for access to its software platform. Pricing is generally based on the number and mix of products subscribed to and the annual construction volume managed on the platform. The company does not charge per-user or per-project fees, and customer support is included at no additional cost.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Procore competes with large aggregated construction management tool providers (such as Oracle, Autodesk, and Trimble), accounting software vendors, point solution providers, and in-house tools developed by customers. It positions itself as a leading, construction-focused, cloud-native platform with broad functionality, deep industry expertise, and a strong ecosystem of integrations.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2022, Procore generated $720.2 million in revenue, up 40% from $514.8 million in 2021, and $400.3 million in 2020. The company reported a net loss of $286.9 million in 2022, reflecting continued investment in growth. Its customer base grew to 14,488 by year-end 2022, with a gross retention rate of 95%.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Procore's value proposition centers on being the system of record for construction, enabling real-time collaboration, data-driven decision-making, and workflow automation across all project stakeholders. Its unlimited user model, open platform with extensive integrations, and deep construction domain expertise differentiate it from competitors, driving productivity, efficiency, and risk reduction for customers.
